samples.summary: New `style.alignment` validation is bypassed by header/footer blocks in the same PUT body
samples.evidence: `assertValidDocsBody` only iterates `body.blocks` (docs-content.controller.ts:249-251), but `writeDocsRoot` also persists `document.header.blocks` and the footer counterpart verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:289-293). A PUT payload carrying `{ blocks: [], header: { marginFromEdge: 0, blocks: [{ id:'b1', type:'paragraph', style:{ alignment: 'center"/><w:jc w:val="right' }, inlines: [] }] } }` reaches Yorkie without ever passing through `assertValidBlockStyle`, and those same blocks are fed to `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` when header1.xml/footer1.xml are generated. The exporter's new `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` clamp is what still saves the file, so the API-level guard the diff advertises is only half-applied. Fix belongs in `assertValidDocsBody`: validate `header`/`footer` blocks too.

samples.summary: Slides PUT arm never validates the docs blocks its text elements carry, so the same alignment guard does not apply there
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlide`/`assertValidElement` (docs-content.controller.ts:376-419) check only element `type`/`frame`; the docs `Block[]` inside a text element's `data.blocks` is written to Yorkie unvalidated. Those blocks flow into `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79` (`ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`), which clamps the value, so the impact is limited to garbage persisted in the deck rather than an injectable attribute — but it is the same guard with a second, unguarded entry point.

samples.summary: PDF export sink was not updated to the new shared color normalizer, so it disagrees with DOCX/PPTX/canvas on cleared and CSS colors
samples.evidence: `styleColor` still does `defaultColorResolver` + a strict `/^#?[0-9a-f]{6}$/` test and returns **black** for anything else (pdf-style-map.ts:143-153). After this change a cleared color (`''`) paints the theme default on canvas and drops the attribute in DOCX/PPTX, but prints solid black in PDF; a pasted `rgb(255, 0, 0)` (which `view/clipboard.ts:150` stores verbatim, and which `toRgbHexColor` now converts for DOCX/PPTX) still prints black in PDF. `pdf-painter.ts:389,635,706,759` and `pdf-table-painter.ts:178` are the affected call sites.
searchedFor: grep styleColor call sites in packages/docs/src/export

samples.summary: Sheets toolbar still resets colors by writing an empty string, now inconsistent with the docs convention this change establishes
samples.evidence: `handleResetTextColor` / `handleResetBgColor` call `spreadsheet?.applyStyle({ tc: "" })` / `{ bg: "" }` (formatting-toolbar.tsx:199-215) while every docs/notes call site was switched to `undefined`. The sheets style model may legitimately treat `""` as its clear sentinel, so this may be intentional; worth confirming it is not the same #728 class of bug in the spreadsheet renderer.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `assertValidDocsBody` (docs-content.controller.ts:239-252) iterates only `body.blocks`; `assertValidBlock`/`assertValidBlockStyle` (:281-295, :266-279) are invoked from just that loop and from table-cell recursion (:322-325). Nothing validates `body.header` / `body.footer`. The PUT body is typed `unknown` (:124) with no DTO, so the global `ValidationPipe` (main.ts:65-72) does not apply. `writeDocsRoot` (docs-tree.ts:517-538) → `buildTreeChildren` (:289-305) maps `document.header.blocks` and `document.footer.blocks` through `buildBlockNode` (:255-259), which spreads `serializeBlockStyle` (:139-150) — that writes `alignment: style.alignment` verbatim with no clamp and no `normalizeBlockStyle` on the write path. `header?`/`footer?` are real fields of the accepted type (yorkie.types.ts:15-21 → packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:15-19), and those same blocks are later rendered into `word/header1.xml`/`footer1.xml` via `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` (docx-exporter.ts:102-124, :186). I looked for any other validation layer on this route (DTO, pipe, interceptor, writer-side normalisation) and found no counterexample: an arbitrary `style.alignment` in a header/footer block reaches the CRDT without passing the new guard. A new guard with a reachable bypass in code the diff does not show is major under this lens; the exporter's `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` map is a separate sink, not the API guard.
